review.finding: _check_no_empty_sections was called against full_body (body + footer), so the LAST heading's content window ran to end-of-string and was masked by the footer's own non-empty link text, silently passing a genuinely empty trailing section.
review.suggestion: Scope the empty-section check to body alone, before the footer is appended.
review.fix: validate() now calls _check_no_empty_sections(body) instead of _check_no_empty_sections(full_body); regression test test_rejects_an_empty_last_heading_even_with_the_footer_appended added.

review.finding: return 0 if result.get("status") == "ok" else 0 — dead ternary, both branches identical.
review.fix: Replaced with `return 0  # non-fatal by contract — the caller reads "status", never the exit code`.

review.finding: Placed under shared/scripts/lib/ despite matching the ADR-045 shape (no intra-package imports, consumed by both shared/scripts/tools/* and a plugin's own scripts/checks/) that the repo's own documented convention (changelog_sections.py's docstring) says belongs at shared/scripts/ top level. The one consumer that imported it as lib.repo_identity (package-qualified) was live evidence of the exact collision risk this convention exists to prevent.
review.suggestion: Move to shared/scripts/repo_identity.py, matching changelog_sections.py's established precedent.
review.fix: Moved to shared/scripts/repo_identity.py with an ADR-045 rationale docstring; updated all five import sites (validate_release_notes.py, create_github_release.py, publish_release_notes.py, setup-changelog.py, test_repo_identity.py) to the top-level import form. Full suite re-run green (68 shared + 87 plugin tests).
